olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n$ with $k$ digits is an \textit{alero} of $m$ if distinct nonzero digits $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ exist (all different from each other and zero) such that adding $a_i$ to the $i$th digit of $m$ gives $n$ (no sum exceeds 9). Find the smallest multiple of 2024 that has an alero also divisible by 2024.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A row of 2024 cells. Ana and Beto alternate (Ana first) placing a digit in an empty cell. The resulting number (ignoring leading zeros) is considered. Beto wins if divisible by 99, else Ana wins. Who wins?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with orthocenter $H$, circumcircle $\Gamma$; $J$ = antipode of $A$. $D,E,F$ = altitude feet. $AP$ meets $\Gamma$ at $P$; circumcircle of $\triangle EFP$ meets $\Gamma$ at $Q$; $K$ = second intersection of $JH$ with $\Gamma$. Prove $K,D,Q$ are collinear.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with incenter $I$, circumcircle $\Gamma$. $D$ = second intersection of $AI$ with $\Gamma$. Line through $I$ parallel to $BC$ meets $AB,AC$ at $P,Q$. $E=PD\cap BC$, $F=QD\cap BC$. Prove $\triangle IEF\sim\triangle ABC$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Positive reals $x,y$ satisfy $\sqrt{x}\left(2+\frac{5}{x+y}\right)=3$ and $\sqrt{y}\left(2-\frac{5}{x+y}\right)=2$. Find the maximum of $x+y$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Cat and mouse play Wim 2 ($n$ stones, remove $1,\ldots,k$ per turn, but not the same number as opponent's last move; player unable to move loses). Find all $k$ such that for every $n$, the cat wins in Wim iff it wins in Wim 2.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2024
